revised.summary:
Revised after review. All 21 critique items were checked against the code. 19 are accepted. Items 7 and 16 are accepted in part, and the rejected part of each is given with its reason in the design's "Review answered" table. Full design: /home/user/Stagewatch/docs/ecosystem/cross-app-proposals.md. Matcher prototype: <scratch>/proto/verbsyntax2.py.

**What the show caller gains.** One place, Stagewatch's shared approval queue, to send lines to every app and to decide what any AI proposes for them.
- **Release A**
  - The operator right-clicks an app in the Show network and sends it a line that app lists, for example "notice Q&A in 2 minutes" to AGMessage or "PLAYLIST CUE show #3" to PlayMap.
  - The same send is the `peer <app> <line>` verb on HTTP (GET with one encoded segment, or a POST JSON body) and WebSocket, and in a Command trigger.
  - The dialog shows the line's risk as it is typed. Every send reports back: sent, then collected, then done or refused. Never just "sent".
  - Pending AI proposals can be approved or rejected from the producer page or the wire with `desk approve|reject <id>`. `next` approves only a non-high item; a high one needs its id and the word `high`.
- **Release B** adds the Stream Deck (Companion), OSC, Stagewatch's copilot planning steps for other apps, and MCP agents proposing to apps. A person always decides.

**What is now safe that was not:**
- A line is never cut and never corrupted. It travels as exactly one argument; quotes, JSON and '/' survive.
- Only a line the target lists is sent, so the PIN is not a relay onto Patterns' admin verbs.
- No key, window address, control character or filled secret placeholder rides any line. PlayMap's `<token>` and `<key>` are refused; the `‹secret›` marker is allowed.
- With no PIN set, `peer` and `desk` work only from this PC or a listed address. This is the sender gate shared with playout-links.
- Proposal ids are unique across Stagewatch restarts (`p17-k3m9`), so no target silently skips a reused id.
- Only verified contexts set risk (after peers-not-screens' G15 fix).
- An unticked step is never approved. A target that has not asked for lines in 15 s is not sent to or approved for.
- Targets see a role word ("operator", "deck"…), not addresses or key names.

**Risk read correctly.** Whole-form matching of each app's listed verbs:
- a value is one word, except a form's last element or a `words`/`line` value;
- carried lines raise the risk;
- PlayMap's RiskWhen and HighFor become rows of their own.

Measured with prototype 2 on PlayMap's 504 examples: 0 rated lower than their row, against 114 of 144 wrong today. A Mapper fixture generated from PlayMap's `RiskOf` fences "never lower than the target".

**Each app**
- **Patterns** lists APPLY and 15 more verbs (Round 90.3), so its assistant's proposals read "review". It refuses an APPLY that it did not propose itself.
- **AGMessage**'s stage line is fixed by the agmessage area (AG-1). This area tests that it parses.
- **PlayMap**:
  - At the round-3 integration pass it publishes its word-dependent risks and which words are secret.
  - Later, once the owner answers decision 7, its assistant can use the desk.
  - Reason corrected: the sink must collect because the engine refuses a shown copy, not because a redacted line would run.

decisions.decision: D1 Rate a line by whole forms of the target's verified table. Pure VerbSyntax/VerbTable in Timer.Core. Literals are case-blind; A|B is one word; […] is optional and nests; a bare … is any words. ' | ' separates forms, and a form not starting with the verb's first word carries the first form's leading literals but the last. Words are read as WireGrammar reads them: a quoted phrase with \" escapes is one word, and a word opening with { or [ runs to the line's end. A <…> value is exactly ONE word, except the form's last element or a value named words, text, line, '… words' or '… line'. Specificity: most literal words, then most single-literal words; an exact tie gives the higher risk; no match or more than 64 words is high. A value named line or '… line' carries a line of the same node: the risk is at least that line's when it names a listed form; words naming no verb add nothing; depth ≤ 4. A JSON value in a row that carries lines is high.
decisions.why: Prototype 2 on Mapper/tests/PlayMap.Engine.Tests/Fleet/Golden/context-busy.json: of 504 form examples, 502 are rated as their row, 2 higher (BIND ADD <json>) and 0 lower. All 35 probe lines hold, including adversarial ones: SCREEN 2 TAKE PVW LOOK x is high; BIND ADD note 60 TO BLACKOUT ON is high, as PlayMap's carried-line rule says (VerbCatalog.cs:826-834, 850-853). Today's prefix matcher (Approvals.cs:225-237, ShowBus.cs:101-102) rates 114 of 144 low/review rows high. The carry rule reproduces PlayMap's VerbSyntax.Alternatives re-prefix (VerbSyntax.cs:21-62).
decisions.alternatives: G02's prefix patch (still ~21 forms wrong). Any value taking any number of words (the first draft): SCREEN 2 TAKE PVW LOOK x would read as the review form. Rejected part of review item 7: a last value absorbing trailing words (MOVE it1 3 BLACKOUT ON → low) is not a mis-rating. Every target names the verb by its leading words, and PlayMap's own RiskOf rates it as MOVE (VerbCatalog.cs:808-813).

decisions.decision: D2 Caps stated and counted. At most 256 commands. A verb over 512 characters is dropped, not cut, and counted; 200 characters of words are kept. A context is at most 64 KiB as sent, counted in UTF-8 bytes. A larger one gets 413 with its size, and the Show network row says so, named by the key's bound node or else by the address. The compiled table is cached per verb list.
decisions.why: A cut verb is a different syntax. Accept counts UTF-16 (ShowBus.cs:60) while the route counts bytes (WebServer.cs:457). Today nobody is told when a context is refused. Measured: PlayMap's busy context is 38,142 bytes compact, about 47.5 KB at 256 rows.
decisions.alternatives: Rejected part of review item 16: the reader cannot trim rows, because it never reads a body past MaxBody (WebServer.cs:1523,1613), which protects the server. Trimming is the sender's duty under spec-1-3's §6 sizes.

decisions.decision: D3 A row whose risk depends on a word lists that form again, with the word written in and its own risk (the §6 rule). PlayMap emits one such row per RiskWhen and HighFor in CommandsFromCatalog (PM-0, the integration pass's file). Mapper generates tests/fixtures/bus/risk-examples.json from RiskOf, and Stagewatch's replay asserts that no PlayMap line is rated lower than PlayMap rates it.
decisions.why: PlayMap's RiskOf raises and lowers by argument (VerbCatalog.cs:47-48,284,350,353,371,390,398,541), but the context emits only v.Risk (Bus/ShowContext.cs:95). Today ASSISTANT SET enabled|provider, DECODE POLICY … FORCE and MACHINE SET GPU-PRIORITY REALTIME rate review on the desk and high on PlayMap. No new notation is needed, and ties already go higher.
decisions.alternatives: Inline per-word notation (every reader must learn it); a 'when' field mirroring RiskWhen (needs the verb name and word indexes); waiting for an owner rewrite of VerbCatalog (it is round 3's spine).

decisions.decision: D4 No secret rides in any line on the desk. Refused at every door (POST /api/proposals, peer, copilot, MCP): a line that fills a secret placeholder with anything but ‹secret›. A placeholder is secret when its whole name is token, key, password, passcode or secret (not pin, which is PlayMap's calibration pin), or when the row's optional "secret": n field marks it (PlayMap's SecretFrom, emitted in PM-0). Also refused anywhere in a line: swk_/agn_ words, a current window token or /w/ followed by a 26-character token, and any control character. A proposer that keeps the secret itself sends ‹secret› and runs its own record. Peer lines never go to Companion's recorder.
decisions.why: PlayMap lists LINK PATTERNS … [<token>] and LINK STAGEWATCH … [<key>] at review (VerbCatalog.cs:249-250; golden rows 72-73). Proposals are readable with a read key (WebServer.cs:604-605,616-617) and ride the frame, MCP and the journal. RunOperatorLine sends RECORD lines to every Companion client (MainViewModel.cs:694-698; CompanionServer.cs:118-122).
decisions.alternatives: Fence only swk_/agn_ (the first draft); fence the 4-digit PIN (false hits on numbers).

decisions.decision: D5 Proposal ids are unique across desk runs: p<n>-<run>. <run> is 4 base-32 characters drawn once per desk start with RandomNumberGenerator. p<n> resolves within the current run. An old run's id gets 404 'this desk restarted since'. Receipts carry refs.sharedProposal as a string, in a new RefIds beside the long Refs.
decisions.why: _next is in memory (Approvals.cs:52,101), and all three targets remember ids across desk restarts and skip a reused one silently: PlayMap StagewatchLink.cs:103,538-541; Patterns StagewatchLinkService.cs:460; AGMessage server.js:1098-1100. CommandReceipt.Refs is long-only (ShowState.cs:1201). MCP's integer ids are local copilot ids (McpEndpoint.cs:153).
decisions.alternatives: A persisted counter (another writer); a time-seeded counter (clock jumps).

decisions.decision: D6 Only verified tables count. They alone set risk, allow a peer send, give quick verbs and reach the model. Verified means posted under a key bound to that id (peers-not-screens NodeBindings, decision 3) or read by Stagewatch's own authenticated link; Patterns' link-read context wins over a posted one. An unverified context rates everything high and never reaches the model. Peers' words reach the model only inside other_apps, which the prompt names as that app's data.
decisions.why: G15: MainViewModel.Desk.cs:65-70 ignores a failed bind, and :81-82 lets a posted context beat the Patterns link's. A forged table would set pre-ticks, copilot steps, born-approved sends and the prompt.
decisions.alternatives: Leave G15 as a risk (the first draft).

decisions.decision: D7 A target may raise the risk of its own proposal, never lower it. When from.id == target.id under a verified binding, the stored risk is max(table, stated).
decisions.why: The table stays the auditable rule, and a self-proposer that knows better can only make its own item safer.
decisions.alternatives: Self-proposers set their own risk (could lower it).

decisions.decision: D8 Refused, never cut. A line is at most 2048 characters; the copilot's 400-character cut becomes a refusal. POST refuses from.t main or mcp, and from.id equal to the desk's id. A peer or desk line aimed at the desk is refused.
decisions.why: Approvals.cs:42,88 and Copilot.cs:189 cut silently. Ref (Approvals.cs:204-211) accepts any kind, so a peer could pose as the desk's operator or as the MCP agent, and bind its key to the desk's id.
decisions.alternatives: Raise the cap and keep cutting.

decisions.decision: D9 The desk observes collection. It records each target's last collect. Stagewatch's own sends, and approvals of pending items, are refused for a target silent for 15 s, with words. The window greys Approve with the reason, and the item stays pending. Proposal JSON shows collected. The rig has options for the window and the fakes' poll.
decisions.why: Targets poll every 2–3 s. A line nobody collects goes undelivered after 60 s (Approvals.cs:44), after the operator believed it sent. Observed state over sent state.
decisions.alternatives: Send or approve anyway and let it go undelivered.

decisions.decision: D10 One pure DeskService (Timer.Show), mirrored by MainViewModel.Desk.cs and hosted by the rig. CommandRisk.Of(ShowCommand) → LineRisk lives in Core (a new enum), and Copilot.Classify maps it. RunWithReceipt saves and restores the outer notes and _executingRemote, and Decide returns the inner outcome.
decisions.why: The rules are tested headless. CopilotRisk lives in Integrations (Copilot.cs:11-20), so Core cannot return it. Nested RunWithReceipt (MainViewModel.Desk.cs:157 inside Receipts.cs:29-38) wipes the outer receipt's refs and errors.
decisions.alternatives: Keep the logic in the view model (no rig e2e).

decisions.decision:
D11 `peer <app> <line>`: a person sends one listed line to another app, born approved.
- Exactly one token follows <app>; more are refused.
- HTTP: a GET form with one URL-encoded segment, and POST /api/peer with {app, line}.
- WS takes args of 2.
- The line must match a listed form of a verified table, hold no secret, be at most 2048 characters and contain no control characters.
- <app> is an id, a unique name, or playmap / patterns / agmessage|messenger when exactly one live app of that kind is heard. stagewatch and main are not app words.
- decidedBy is a role word (operator, operator (copilot), wire, deck, trigger); the key name and address go only to the desk's journal.
- Who may send is decided by playout-links' sender gate (PlayoutGate, Remote.PlayoutFrom), extended to Peer and Desk.
  - HTTP and WS: a PIN that is set and given, or a control key.
  - With no PIN: this PC or a listed address only.
  - OSC and Companion (release B): this PC or a listed address.
  - Never a node, read or MCP key, and never as a proposal.
  - Triggers may send (origin: this PC).
- The receipt waits within 3 s through playout-links' ReceiptNotes.Peer, and WS and Companion get its final follow-up.
decisions.why: CheckPin passes an empty PIN (WebServer.cs:870), and WS role=control then controls (:1149,1191). Every tokenizer drops quotes (McpEndpoint.cs:173-185, CloudAdvisor.cs:163-179); HTTP splits on '/' before unescaping (:792); Companion turns \n into a newline (CompanionProtocol.cs:73). Patterns runs approved lines as a wire client (AppServices.cs:682-686), with RESTART <passcode> and UPDATE APPLY on its wire (Patterns docs/REMOTE.md:87-88). AGMessage shows decidedBy to every meeting (server.js:1073). No Stagewatch collects as a target (WebServer.cs:575,600). Fail closed: an unknown word is refused.
decisions.alternatives: Unlisted lines rated high (the first draft: a relay onto every admin verb); a pending item for the operator's own line (ceremony); only the loopback bind as the Companion/OSC gate (shuts out a Companion PC).

decisions.decision: D12 `desk approve <id> [high]`, `desk approve next`, `desk reject <id>|next [<why…>]`. next approves only a non-high oldest item; a high item needs its id and the word high. Refused for a silent target (D9). The same sender gate as peer. Refused from MCP, triggers, the advisor, copilot steps and proposals. The deck approves the id it shows (desk_next_id); a high item takes a second press, which sends HIGH.
decisions.why: Triggers run lines with no transport gate (Triggers.cs:56,81; MainViewModel.Integrations.cs:59), which would let automation approve AI proposals unseen. A blind next could approve a high item.
decisions.alternatives: next for everything; a rig-only stdin approve.

decisions.decision: D13 Approving a shared proposal honours the tick: an unticked step is not approved.
decisions.why: ApproveProposal sends any shared item to ApproveShared (MainViewModel.Copilot.cs:165, Desk.cs:135-159), although a high step is never pre-ticked (Copilot.cs:25).
decisions.alternatives: None; it is a defect.

decisions.decision:
D14 (release B) The copilot plans for other apps.
- A step gains a target.
- other_apps gives id, collects, verified and verb_heads (2,840 bytes for PlayMap).
- Full verbs come only when the request names the app, or the plan asks need_verbs (at most one second pass, ≤32 KB per app and ≤64 KB in total, with more_verbs counted).
- A step is kept only when it is listed and secret-free; it is rated by the table; over 2048 characters is refused.
- Run ticked steps runs in order through a pure PlanRunner. An app step waits up to 10 s for its result; a refusal or no result stops the run. Each run of Stagewatch steps is its own undo batch.
- Dropped words are per app.
- ShowCommandParser.Help, which the AIs read, leaves peer and desk out; PersonHelp lists them.
decisions.why: Measured cost: 32,843 bytes of PlayMap commands on every request versus 2,840 bytes of heads. Today Help goes into the prompt and MCP's tool text (Copilot.cs:74; McpEndpoint.cs:87,139). Order across apps must hold: attempts are not facts.
decisions.alternatives: Every app's full table on every request (the first draft); app steps sent asynchronously after Stagewatch's.

decisions.decision: D15 (release B) MCP: run_command.target always makes a pending shared proposal from {t:mcp}, even with direct agents. get_proposal takes string ids. get_context.peer returns verified contexts only. peer and desk lines are isError.
decisions.why: Another app's approval is not Stagewatch's to waive.
decisions.alternatives: Honour AgentsNeedApproval for app targets.

decisions.decision: D16 The desk's door (WPF, the maintainer's PC). The Show network row's right-click and its '…' button offer the same items: Send a line…, up to 6 quick verbs, Its verbs…, Copy headline. The dialog calls DeskService.Send with the raw string and shows the form, risk, words and collect state. Items are greyed with reasons (not collecting, unverified).
decisions.why: G14 and G20; desk buttons and right-click stay in step; the raw string avoids Q()'s quote rewrite (MainViewModel.cs:119) and the recorder.
decisions.alternatives: A messenger-only 'Send notice'.

decisions.decision: D17 Every reader. The operator frame gets desk{pending, next, apps}. /api/config and Companion CONFIG get peers. Companion gets an ACCESS line per connection (release B). The producer page gets a desk panel: approve and reject by id, with a high item confirmed. The context's peers[] rows get collects. The AI facts and the papers follow.
decisions.why: The operator frame would carry desk with no page to act on it (producer.js reads the operator frame). The module must know whether its port may drive other apps.
decisions.alternatives: WPF-only approval.

decisions.decision: D18 Two releases, each complete in its papers. A: D1–D13, D16, and D17 without ACCESS. B: Companion and OSC doors with the module, D14 and D15.
decisions.why: Review item 17: ship the fences and the approve-by-id flow on HTTP/WS first. The papers name what B adds and why it waits (the brief's 'say which reader it did not reach').
decisions.alternatives: One release of 13 units across 4 repos.

decisions.decision:
D19 PlayMap.
- PM-0, in the integration pass: derived risk rows, the secret field and risk-examples.json in Core/Bus/ShowContext.cs (§5.6 item 7).
- PM-1, after W4, the integration pass and the owner's decision 7: NetworkHost publishes the desk; the sink collects (CollectApproved=true) and the link's pull pauses.
  - The reason, corrected: with the link collecting, PlayMap's own secret-bearing proposals would be refused as shown copies (EngineCore.cs:330).
  - Orphaned forwarded proposals fail with words after a switch-off or restart.
  - STATE assistant.desk gets one ran counter with its collector.
  - ASSISTANT SET desk auto|off comes with the NetworkDrawer toggle and right-click (DeskVerbRuleTests), and Companion verbs.json is regenerated.
decisions.why: Review item 9; Mapper docs/round3/PLAN.md:2135 (ShowContext.cs is the integration pass's), :2185 (EngineCore.Assistant.cs is workflows' in W4). Neither counter reaches STATE today (StagewatchLink.cs:144; StagewatchProposalSink.cs:85).
decisions.alternatives: CollectApproved=false as CARRYOVER.md:99 says (own secret proposals refused).

decisions.decision:
D20 Patterns Round 90.3 (the numbering patterns-playmap-side gives).
- Append 16 rows: APPLY review, worded 'only this desk's own'; WEB KEY <key name>, so it is not read as a secret; WEB CLICK listed; WEB OPEN and WEB TYPE not listed.
- StagewatchLinkService runs APPLY only when p.FromId == SelfId and Approvals.ByDesk(p.Id) is the record whose local id the line names.
decisions.why: LocalId ignores from (ShowBusNodes.cs:233-240), and RunAsync applies whoever proposed (StagewatchLinkService.cs:482-495), so a rejected proposal could come back pre-ticked from another node. WEB OPEN can carry a window's pass (G09/G10), and WEB TYPE text can be a password.
decisions.alternatives: Rate APPLY high unless from.id == target.id on the desk (Patterns' own fence is the authority).

decisions.decision: D21 AGMessage: no unit here. agmessage AG-1 (0.5.0) owns `message "<text>" <urgency> off ack` via proposeStageLine (design/agmessage.md:120-121). SW-2's test proves the line parses and the old one fails. Role-word decidedBy reaches its meetings with no AGMessage change.
decisions.why: One owner per AGMessage change; G05 closes with AG-1 plus SW-2.
decisions.alternatives: A separate 0.4.1 (the first draft).

revised.wire:
STAGEWATCH GRAMMAR
New kinds ShowCommandKind.Peer and .Desk, appended after the last kind (playout-links' Playout if it lands first).
  peer <app> <line>
  desk approve <id> [high] | desk approve next
  desk reject <id>|next [<why…>]
<line> is exactly one token. <app> is one of:
- a node id;
- a unique name (case-blind);
- playmap, patterns or agmessage|messenger, when exactly one live app of that kind is heard.

Transports (A = release A, B = release B):
- HTTP (A):
  - GET|POST /api/peer/<app>/<one URL-encoded line>; more segments → 400.
  - POST /api/peer with Content-Type application/json, body {"app":"pm-a1b2","line":"SET out1 name \"Left wall\""} (≤16 KB).
  - /api/desk/approve/p17, /api/desk/approve/p18-k3m9/high, /api/desk/reject/next/<why>.
- WS (A): {"cmd":"peer","args":["pm-a1b2","PLAYLIST CUE \"Main show\" #3"],"id":"a1"}. A message is at most 4096 bytes; longer lines go by HTTP POST.
- Companion TCP (B): @c1 PEER "PlayMap Hall" "SET out1 name \"Left wall\"", @c2 DESK APPROVE p18-k3m9 HIGH, @c3 DESK REJECT NEXT "not now".
- OSC (B): /stagewatch/peer ,ss pm-a1b2 "…"; /stagewatch/desk/approve ,s p17.
- Command trigger (A): peer only, origin this PC. A line with inner quotes is refused, never altered.
- MCP: run_command with a peer or desk line → isError.

AUTH (playout-links' sender gate, PlayoutGate + Remote.PlayoutFrom, extended to Peer and Desk; labelled "May drive other show apps from"):
- HTTP and WS: a PIN that is set and given, or a control key. With no PIN set: only from loopback or a listed address; otherwise 403 {"ok":false,"error":"peer and desk act on other apps with a person's authority — set a PIN, use a control key, or add this address under Remote → May drive other apps"}.
- OSC and Companion: loopback or a listed address.
- Node, read and MCP keys: 403.
- desk is refused from triggers, the advisor, copilot steps, MCP and proposals: "a person approves — not a trigger, the copilot or an agent".

REFUSALS (receipt error and status line)
- parse: "peer takes an app and one line — quote the line as one argument"
- parse: "desk takes approve or reject"
- parse: "desk approve takes a proposal id (p17) or next"
- "no app called 'pm' on the show network — heard: …"
- "two apps answer 'playmap' — name one: …"
- "PlayMap Hall does not list 'OUTPUTS OFF' — see its verbs"
- "PlayMap Hall's verbs are not verified (posted without its key) — Stagewatch sends only lines it can read"
- "PlayMap Hall has not asked this desk for approved lines in 40 s — it would not collect this"
- "a secret rides in no line — type it on PlayMap Hall itself"
- "a key rides in no line"
- "a window's address rides in no line"
- "a line is at most 2048 characters"
- "a line holds no control characters"
- "p18 is high — approve it by its id: desk approve p18-k3m9 high"

Risk: CommandRisk.Of (Core, LineRisk) rates both kinds High. Neither is in ShowContext.Commands, nor in ShowCommandParser.Help (AI-facing). PersonHelp lists them.

RECEIPTS (Show Bus §3, X-Request-Id)
200 {"type":"receipt","id":"a1","ok":true,"stage":"applied","effect":"PlayMap Hall ran PLAYLIST CUE show #3: cued Intro (p17)","error":null,"refs":{"sharedProposal":"p17-k3m9"}}
200 {…"stage":"accepted","effect":"sent to PlayMap Hall as p17 — it collects every 2 s and reports back",…,"refs":{"sharedProposal":"p17-k3m9"}}
409 {…"ok":false,"error":"PlayMap Hall refused PLAYLIST CUE show #9: Show has no item #9 (p17)","refs":{"sharedProposal":"p17-k3m9"}}
- refs merges the existing long refs with the new string RefIds (CommandReceipt gains RefIds, appended).
- An accepted receipt is followed on WS and Companion by playout-links' "final":true receipt. That is §3 text carried by spec-1-3; this area adds none.

SHARED QUEUE (Show Bus §11)
- Ids are p<n>-<run>, e.g. p17-k3m9. p<n> resolves within the current run. GET /api/proposals/<another run's id> → 404 {"ok":false,"error":"no such proposal — this desk restarted since (run k3m9)"}.
- POST /api/proposals: the body and auth are unchanged. 400 with words for:
  - a line over 2048 characters (never cut);
  - a control character;
  - a swk_/agn_ word, a window token or /w/ followed by a 26-character token;
  - a filled secret placeholder (anything but ‹secret›);
  - from.t main or mcp, or from.id equal to the desk's id;
  - a peer or desk line aimed at the desk.
- The reply appends fields: {"ok":true,"id":"p17-k3m9","state":"pending","risk":"review","form":"UNDO","formWords":"Undoes the last edit"}.
- Proposal JSON appends "collected" (unix ms|null) and "form", before agmessage's "delivery".
- GET ?target=<id>&state=approved also records that id's last collect.
- Risk: the most specific full form of a verified table (literals, then single literals); an exact tie goes higher; carried lines raise it; no match is high. A bound self-proposal gets max(table, stated).
- Born-approved lines are from {"t":"main","id":<desk id>,"name":<room>}, with state "approved" and decidedBy one of "operator", "operator (copilot)", "wire", "deck", "trigger". The key name and address go only to the desk's journal.
- MCP proposals for an app are from {"t":"mcp","id":"mcp","name":"AI agent (MCP)"} and are always pending.

§6 NOTATION (words for spec-1-3 S1, 1.3; copies byte-identical under the body hash)
- Literals are case-blind; A|B is one word.
- <…> is one word; a form's last element, or a value named words, text, line, '… words' or '… line', takes one or more.
- […] is optional; a bare … is any words; ' | ' separates forms, which carry the leading literals.
- A quoted phrase is one word; a word opening with { or [ runs to the line's end.
- A word-dependent risk is a row of its own.
- A placeholder named token, key, password, passcode or secret holds a secret, and so do the words from n on when a row has the optional field "secret": n (appended to the row).
- At most 256 commands; a verb ≤512 is dropped, not cut; at least 200 characters of words are kept.

COPILOT (B, model I/O)
- A step is {command, why, target}; target "" means Stagewatch.
- The plan may add "need_verbs":[id] (one second pass).
- other_apps[] is {app, id, name, collects, verified, light, headline, verb_heads[], verbs?[{verb,risk,words≤100}], more_verbs}.

MCP (B)
- run_command adds target:string → "Queued for the operator's approval as p17-k3m9 (risk review, form …). get_proposal {\"id\":\"p17-k3m9\"} follows it."
- get_proposal.id is integer|string.
- get_context adds peer (verified contexts only, else isError).
- initialize.instructions gains one sentence.

FRAMES, CONFIG, CONTEXT (new fields at the end)
- Operator frame and Companion SNAPSHOT (never public): "desk":{"pending":2,"next":{"id":"p18-k3m9","from":"AI agent (MCP)","target":"PlayMap Hall","line":"UNDO","risk":"review","collects":true},"apps":[{"id":"pm-a1b2","name":"PlayMap Hall","kind":"playmap","collects":true,"verified":true}]}. next.line is ≤120 characters.
- /api/config and Companion CONFIG: "peers":[{"id","name","kind"}].
- Companion (B): per connection, after SUBSCRIBE JSON and whenever the gate changes: ACCESS {"peer":true,"desk":true,"why":""}.

issues.issue: `peer` and `desk` work over HTTP and WS with no PIN at all. When no PIN is configured, any host on the LAN can send born-approved lines. Patterns runs them as a paired wire client and PlayMap runs them in its Approved role. This is the same pairing bypass the design uses to justify the loopback gate on Companion and OSC, but HTTP and WS are left open.
issues.fix: Refuse `peer`/`desk` unless a PIN is set or a control key is used. With no PIN, allow them only from loopback. Add a test with an empty PIN on HTTP and on WS role=control.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/WebServer.cs:870 (CheckPin returns null when the PIN is empty); :1163,1191 (WS role=control gets CanControl with no PIN); :804-806 (the generic path only asks for Control); Patterns/src/Patterns.App/Services/AppServices.cs:682-686 (approved lines go to Router as OriginKind.Tcp); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Show/ShowPolicy.cs:35-36

issues.issue: `peer` sends unlisted lines, only rated high. That turns Stagewatch's 4-digit PIN, which locks out per IP, into full wire control of Patterns and PlayMap, admin verbs included: Patterns `RESTART <passcode>`, `UPDATE APPLY <passcode>`, `DEVICE * …`, `OUTPUTS OFF`. It also breaks Stagewatch's own doctrine ('an unknown word is refused, never defaulted').
issues.fix: Fail closed: `peer` sends only lines that match a listed form of the target's verified table and refuses anything else with words. A target can widen this with an advertised opt-in (a §6 flag), never by the desk's default.
issues.evidence: Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md (RESTART/UPDATE APPLY rows); design decision 7 ('Unlisted lines are allowed for a person, rated high'); Stagewatch/CLAUDE.md doctrine 'Fail closed on the wire'

issues.issue: The secret fence covers only swk_/agn_ keys and window tokens. Peer-native secrets pass it. Examples: PlayMap `LINK PATTERNS <host> [<token>]` (Patterns' pairing token, row 72, rated review), and Patterns `RESTART <passcode>` / `UPDATE APPLY <passcode>`. These then sit in the queue and the journal, in GET /api/proposals (read scope), in the frame's desk.next, in MCP get_state and get_proposal, and in the Companion recorder if the send dialog goes through RunOperatorLine, which broadcasts to every Companion client.
issues.fix: Refuse a line whose matched form has a secret placeholder (<token>|<key>|<passcode>|<password>), or have §6 rows say which word starts the secret. PlayMap already knows this per verb (VerbSpec.SecretFrom, VerbCatalog.Redacted). Never pass peer lines to RecordUi. Test with LINK PATTERNS and RESTART lines.

issues.issue: Rebuilding the `peer` line by re-joining tokens corrupts it silently. Every Stagewatch tokenizer drops `"` and the parser joins the remaining tokens with spaces, so `SET out1 name "Left wall"` becomes `SET out1 name Left wall` and `ADD media {"path": "a b.mp4"}` becomes invalid JSON. The app's own line builder Q() turns quotes into apostrophes. HTTP joins extra path segments with spaces, so an unencoded '/' turns into a space. Companion's `\n` escape puts a newline into the line, and ProposeApproved skips Submit's control-character strip. All of this contradicts the design's own 'refused, never cut'.
issues.fix: Treat the line as exactly one argument: refuse when more than one token follows <app>. The send dialog and the copilot call DeskService.Send with the raw string, never a built grammar line. Refuse control characters. Add round-trip tests for quoted, JSON and '/' lines on HTTP, WS, Companion, OSC and triggers.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/McpEndpoint.cs:180; Timer.Companion/CompanionProtocol.cs:71-78; Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs:119 (Q); MainViewModel.Systems.cs:751-756 (RunCommandLine tokenizes); WebServer.cs:791-792 (split on '/', then unescape)

issues.issue: Proposal ids start again at p1 every time Stagewatch starts, but every target remembers ids across desk runs. After a Stagewatch restart mid-show, a `peer` line or an approved AI proposal that reuses an id a target already ran is skipped with no result posted. The desk shows it collected, then 'didn't report back' 5 minutes later. The design makes this queue the operator's main command path, and its 15 s freshness check gives false confidence.
issues.fix: Make ids unique across desk runs (for example a run-epoch prefix, still opaque under §11), and add a restart test against all three collectors. Then refs.proposal cannot be a long; make it a string.

issues.issue: G15 has to block this work, not sit in the risks list. The design makes the posted table decide four things: pre-ticking, which copilot app steps are kept, what a born-approved Run sends, and the model's prompt (verbs plus `words` of up to 200 characters × 256 rows, untrusted text). A forged context can list `BLACKOUT ON` as low for Patterns' id. The copilot then proposes it pre-ticked and 'Run ticked steps' sends it born-approved. RiskFor also prefers a posted context over the authenticated Patterns link's context.
issues.fix: Make SW-1 and SW-5 depend on the peers-not-screens units: decision 3 (NodeBindings checked before storing) and decision 8 (unverified contexts never set risk). Prefer the link-read context for Patterns. Mark peers' `words` as untrusted data in the prompt, or leave them out.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Desk.cs:65-70 (BindKey false ignored), :81-82 (posted context wins over _patterns.Context); scratchpad/design/peers-not-screens.md decisions 3 and 8

issues.issue: '0 wrong, never lower' only holds against the context rows, and only on self-generated canonical examples where every value is the single word 'x1'. First, PlayMap raises risk by argument (RiskWhen), and the context publishes only the row's risk: `MACHINE SET GPU-PRIORITY REALTIME` and `DECODE POLICY DIRECT FORCE` rate review (pre-ticked, born-approved) where PlayMap says High. Second, a `<x>` placeholder takes one or more words, so trailing words are absorbed: running the prototype gives `MOVE it1 3 BLACKOUT ON` = low, `PROJECT SAVE x BLACKOUT ON` = low, `UNDO TO 5 BLACKOUT ON` = review.
issues.fix: Only a form's last value, or an explicit `…`, may take several words; every other `<x>` is one word. Carry per-argument risk in §6: PlayMap emits a raised row per RiskWhen through the integration pass or the spine lane, and ties already go higher. Add adversarial lines and RiskWhen lines to the golden replay.
issues.evidence: Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Wire/VerbCatalog.cs:350,541 (RiskWhen FORCE and REALTIME → High); Mapper/src/PlayMap.Core/Bus/ShowContext.cs:95 (only v.Risk is emitted); proto/verbsyntax.py match(): 'val' loops k over wi+1..len(words); reproduced with the prototype on context-busy.json

issues.issue: Approval without a person. `desk approve` passes 'the same gate as peer', but Command triggers and assistant paths run grammar lines with no transport gate, so a trigger `desk approve next` approves AI proposals sight unseen. That breaks §11 ('a human approves') and the design's 'an AI never approves'. The deck's `desk approve next` is also blind: it approves whatever is oldest at press time, a high item included, with no tick, while the window insists on the tick.
issues.fix: Refuse `desk` from triggers, the advisor and the copilot. The deck approves by id (a desk_next_id variable) and is refused when that id is no longer the next one or was already decided. A high item takes a second press or is refused for `next`.

issues.issue: The design's claim about PlayMap is wrong. CollectApproved=false would not 'run ‹secret› lines'. The engine refuses any shown copy before running it ('this is a shown copy … never runs'), and the link's CommandRunner goes through the engine endpoint. With the link collecting, PlayMap's own secret-bearing proposals would fail; they would not run redacted. The conclusion (the sink collects) still holds, but CARRYOVER's answer and the PM-1 test need the true reason. A different hole is untested: proposals forwarded before a switch-off or restart lose their record and then fail. Collector counters also move (the link's _approvalsRun vs the sink's Ran).
issues.fix: Restate the reason ('own secret-bearing proposals would be refused as shown copies'). Test that an orphaned forwarded proposal fails with words after switch-off or restart. Keep STATE's approval counters consistent across the switch.

issues.issue: The design writes into §11 that `from.t` may be `main` or `mcp` on the wire. Any node key or PIN holder can then POST `{from:{t:'main',id:<desk id>}}` or `{t:'mcp',name:'AI agent (MCP)'}` and appear as the desk's own operator or copilot, or as the MCP agent: a peer acting as another. Submit would also bind that node key to the desk's id.
issues.fix: Refuse from.t main or mcp, and from.id equal to the desk's id, on POST /api/proposals. Only DeskService creates those internally. Add a test.

issues.issue: The Patterns APPLY row is rated review whoever proposes it. Patterns applies `APPLY <localId>` without checking who proposed it, so another node can re-propose a Patterns proposal the operator rejected, and it now arrives pre-ticked.
issues.fix: Rate APPLY review only when from.id == target.id with a bound key (otherwise high), or have Patterns check FromId == SelfId. Fence it in Patterns' round.

issues.issue: decidedBy values such as 'PIN 10.0.0.7' and 'key <name>' go verbatim to targets. AGMessage shows them to every open meeting ('approved by …'), and those meetings can include people off-site through the tunnel. That leaks the desk's addresses and key names.
issues.fix: Send targets a role word ('operator', 'operator (copilot)', 'deck', 'trigger') and keep the details in the desk's journal.

issues.issue: The `peer` app words include stagewatch/main, but no Stagewatch ever collects as a target, so the freshness check always refuses and `main` can resolve to this desk itself.
issues.fix: Drop stagewatch/main from `<app>` resolution.
issues.evidence: grep: 'state=approved' appears in Stagewatch src only in WebServer's serve path; MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:100

issues.issue: A `desk approve` of a desk-targeted proposal nests receipts. ApproveShared calls RunWithReceipt inside the outer RunWithReceipt, but _receipt and _executingRemote are single fields reset in finally, so the outer receipt loses its refs, errors and handed-on state.
issues.fix: Decide returns the inner outcome. The desk-target run goes through a non-receipt executor, or the receipt notes become a stack.

issues.issue: The copilot path breaks the design's own rules and the plan's order. ParsePlan silently cuts commands at 400 characters. 'Run ticked steps' runs Stagewatch steps at once while app steps land 0–3 s later, so the order across apps is not kept. PlanConsequence and the Dropped text assume Stagewatch grammar. ShowCommandParser.Help, which goes into the copilot prompt and the MCP tool description, will advertise peer/desk to the AIs.
issues.fix: Refuse over-long commands instead of cutting them. Either state that app steps are asynchronous or run steps in order and wait for each result. Leave peer/desk out of the Help given to AIs. Write separate Dropped words for app steps.

issues.issue: A context over 64 KB is refused whole, which interacts badly with the 256/512/200 caps. PlayMap's busy context is already 43.6 KB at 199 rows. At round 3's rows and longer words it can pass 64 KB, and then everything is lost: every risk reads high, the light and the headline go, and nobody is told. The cap also counts UTF-16 characters, not bytes.
issues.fix: State the byte cap next to the row caps in §6 and trim rows (counting the dropped) rather than refusing the whole context. Count UTF-8 bytes. Coordinate with the spec-1-3 sizes table.

issues.issue: The cost of the copilot brief is measured in bytes but not governed by need: about 30–33 KB (roughly 8–10k tokens) is added to every copilot request while PlayMap is linked, whatever the request is about. More generally this is over-building: 13 units in 4 repos, `peer` on 5 transports, plus copilot targets, an MCP target, quick verbs and a send dialog.
issues.fix: Include an app's verbs only when the request names that app, or in a second pass. Ship a smaller first cut (the matcher, the tick fix, the send dialog plus `peer` on HTTP/WS with the PIN, the AGMessage and Patterns rows) and leave copilot/MCP targets and Companion/OSC transports for a later step.

issues.issue: Ambiguous ids and field names. refs.proposal=17 (a long) clashes with MCP get_proposal's integer ids, which are local CopilotProposal ids. The POST reply's new `words` (the form's description) clashes with the proposal JSON's `words`, which is the target's result.
issues.fix: Use a string ref ("p17") under its own name, and name the reply field `formWords`.

issues.issue: Gaps in the spec and process text. A `final:true` follow-up receipt is a §3 change that is not in the §2.6 SHOWBUS edits, and the Companion module would get two OK lines per id. The rule 'Patterns' copy word for word but the model name' conflicts with spec-1-3's byte-identical body hash. The version bump to 1.3 is not stated.
issues.fix: List the §3 change or drop the follow-up receipt. Align the copy rule with spec-1-3 and name the version.

issues.issue: Some tests are weak or will break. The e2e accepts either 'applied' or 'accepted then done', so it does not prove the awaited-result seam. It also waits 16 s of real time. Its fake peers must collect with node keys once peers-not-screens refuses the PIN for bound ids. Changing Submit's signature breaks the existing DeskRules calls unless an overload is kept. CommandRisk.Of in Core cannot return CopilotRisk, which is an Integrations type.
issues.fix: Use a rig option for the freshness window and the poll interval so a single outcome can be asserted. Keep the old Submit overload. Move the risk enum to Core.

issues.issue: The Companion/OSC loopback gate leaves the deck with no path whenever Companion runs on another PC (bound to all interfaces), and the module cannot know this until a press fails. The URL-path HTTP form also cannot carry a 2048-character quoted line inside the 8192-byte header cap.
issues.fix: Put a flag in CONFIG saying whether peer/desk are allowed on this port so the module greys its actions out. Accept the line in a POST body for /api/peer.

missing: A blocking dependency on peers-not-screens (G15) decisions 3 and 8: only verified contexts set risk, feed the copilot or decide a born-approved send; the authenticated Patterns link context is preferred.
Proposal ids unique across Stagewatch restarts (all three targets remember ids across desk runs), with a restart test.
A policy for no PIN: `peer`/`desk` refused, or loopback only, when no PIN is set.
Per-argument risk (PlayMap's RiskWhen) carried in §6 rows, plus the one-word-per-placeholder rule and adversarial replay lines.
Per-verb secret awareness for peer-native secrets (Patterns' pairing token, RESTART/UPDATE passcodes), and keeping peer lines out of the Companion recorder.
A gate keeping `desk approve` away from triggers and automation; the deck approves by id, not `next`.
The browser pages chain: no Producer/Showcaller page shows or decides the shared queue, though the operator frame now carries `desk`.

PlayMap chains for ASSISTANT SET desk: the Avalonia desk's menu and right-click door (MenuCoverageTests), regenerated Companion verbs.json and fixtures, and the fact that EngineCore.Assistant.cs belongs to wp3-workflows in W4.

Rows for Patterns WEB TYPE/CLICK, or an explicit 'not listed and why'; the APPLY row limited to self-proposals.
